verdicts.rewritten_summary: UK Home Office country policy note on Russia (June 2025, assessment section updated 11 June 2025) - the parent-framework document a visitor here stands under: same-sex activity is not criminalised but same-sex marriage and gender transition are banned, trans-specific healthcare was effectively banned in 2023, and no discrimination legislation based on sexual orientation or gender identity covers housing, healthcare or employment. 'Gay propaganda' offences carry fines up to 400,000 roubles (about £3,600) for individuals or up to 15 days' detention, repeat offences can bring criminal prosecution with up to four years in prison, and the November 2023 Supreme Court 'extremist' designation of the international LGBT+ movement makes participation punishable by 2-6 years and organising by 6-10 years. Between December 2022 and March 2024 at least 139 people were affected by enforcement of anti-LGBT+ laws, and the note assesses trans people, publicly active LGBT+ advocates and those in the North Caucasus as likely to face treatment amounting to persecution. No region-specific findings: the document sets the national conditions in force across all of Russia, this region included.

HRW report (30 June 2025): Russian courts issued 101 'extremism'-related convictions - approximately 98 administrative and three criminal - tied to the 'International Public LGBT Movement' designation; the Supreme Court ruling of November 2023 entered into force in January 2024 and opened the way to arbitrary prosecutions of LGBT people and their supporters. Between January 2024 and June 2025 at least 20 people faced criminal charges under the designation (two sentenced to prison; one died by suicide in pretrial detention), and 81 people in 98 court cases were found guilty of administrative offences for displaying banned symbols, with fines up to 2,000 roubles and repeat displays punishable under the criminal code by up to four years in prison. On 15 May 2025 investigators charged three publishing-house staff under article 282.2 for selling fiction exploring LGBT themes, facing up to 12 years. No region-specific findings; documents the national enforcement climate governing visitors across all Russian regions.
